concept: The Power of Community Health Education and Referral
rationale: The testimonials consistently highlight the importance of community health education in identifying health issues and the role of community health workers in referring individuals to appropriate healthcare facilities. This concept is seen in the workers' encounters with community members suffering from various health issues, including STIs, mental health problems, and physical injuries.
examples: Millicent Randiki: I came across a young mother and some two men who really wanted to talk to me privately concerning the topic. I talked to them, counseled them and then I referred them to the nearest center.
Imelda Anyango: I told her maybe it could be a dislocation but she has to go to the health facility.
Milka Nyadiang'a: I gave him counseling and later referred him to Airport Hospital for more diagnosis and counseling.

Lency Mmbone: After I visited them and talked to them that failing is not the end of the world, it depends on what are you planning to do with your life and also did referral to the hospital at Migosi so that they are counseled more.

concept: Bridging the Gap: Community Health Workers as Health Educators and Advocates
rationale: Across the testimonials, community health workers consistently play a crucial role in educating community members about various health conditions, dispelling myths, and advocating for appropriate medical care. They bridge the gap between medical knowledge and community understanding, often leading to improved health outcomes.
examples: Daniel Ayieko: With my help, I referred the ??? to take the child to the hospital. The child was tested and was found to be ailing from asthma.
Imelda Anyango: I taught her that signs/symptoms may be the same at times, but we can't tell whether it is malaria or COVID-19 without being tested.
Liz Adhiambo: I told her that vaccination prevents individuals from infections of diseases, e.g. small pox, measles, TB & polio.
Bunnyce Atieno: When I taught them about polio she cried and shouted and asked me why we did not teach them early enough.
Pauline Adhiambo: After she was discharged I continued educating the mother on the causes, signs and symptoms and also preventive measures to take so that the same doesn't repeat itself next time.

concept: Empowerment through Health Education and Services
rationale: Across the testimonials, community health workers consistently emphasize the importance of educating community members about various health issues, particularly HIV/AIDS, and providing necessary health services. This education and service provision empowers individuals and communities to take control of their health, leading to improved outcomes.
examples: Emily Ayua: I created awareness on blood pressure, HIV/AIDS, Malaria, and many other diseases. I encouraged the audience on knowing their blood pressure and HIV/AIDS status.
Joseph Ochieng: The Community Health Workers also provide health education under the slogan "Community Health (supports) with Knowledge. All the services are absolutely free.

Millicent Randiki Okoth: After counselling, I referred him to the nearest health facility, where he could get the services. After 3 days of follow-ups, I found out that he was tested and given condoms.
Lency Mmbone: They said that they didn't know more about HIV/AIDS and after being empowered they can empower their fellows also.

concept: The Importance of Water Treatment Education
rationale: Across the testimonials, a common theme is the critical role of community health workers in educating communities about the importance of water treatment to prevent waterborne diseases. This education is often delivered in response to observed health issues, such as typhoid, diarrhea, and stomach aches, which are linked to the consumption of untreated water.
examples: Liz Odhiambo: I told them that it is not a must to use water-guard, but we have cheap processes to use like boiling to sixty minutes, and exposing water to the sun to kill dangerous agents in water.

Pauline Adhiambo: I always advise most household members who are experiencing that not to visit places such as swimming pools until they get better and also to take their babies to be vaccinated against rotovirus.
Tracy Agatha Achieng': Awareness has been the main key. This encourages a lot of people to avoid risks.

Bunnyce Atieno: Cholera is so rampant and this is due to this ignorance so in the field I taught my community members that they should treat water no matter where thy draw it from so as to prevent them from getting waterborne diseases.
Milka Nyadiang'a: He agreed to ever use boiled or treated water for drinking and always wash fruits with running water before eating them.

concept: Community Health Workers as COVID-19 Educators and Advocates
rationale: Across the testimonials, a common theme is the role of community health workers (CHWs) in educating their communities about COVID-19, advocating for preventive measures, and supporting their communities through the pandemic. They are actively involved in sensitizing the community about the virus, promoting hygiene practices, and encouraging vaccination. They also express satisfaction when they see positive changes in their communities as a result of their efforts.
examples: Daniel Ayieko: Having trained as a Community Health Worker, I have been actively sensitizing and creating awareness to my community members on the preventive measures against the COVID-19 pandemic.

Pauline Adhiambo: CHW's have really been pressuring that the communities follow the steps that were laid by the county government of Kisumu—such as social distancing, wearing face masks, washing hands, staying at home while sick and others.
Zachary Omondi: As trained Community Health Workers, we have been in the frontline in helping the government and other stakeholders in implementing these policies.

Imelda Anyango: As a Community Health Worker, following the WHO directives, I protect myself first. I make sure that I wear a mask, before and after the task. I sanitize. I create awareness on COVID-19 by teaching people what COVID-19 is, how it spreads, signs and symptoms, then preventive measures like wearing masks, washing hands at all times, avoiding over crowded places and also maintaining social distancing.

Julliet Omollo: As a CHW, I have been creating door-to-door awareness. I have also conducted health education to students and pupils on COVID-19. I have also conducted education to women groups and men. I have created awareness to chiefs office.

concept: Empowerment through Knowledge and Intervention
rationale: The testimonials consistently highlight the role of community health workers in educating individuals about their rights, the nature of abuse, and the resources available to them. They also intervene directly in situations of abuse, providing advice, emotional support, and referrals to appropriate authorities or organizations. This dual role of education and intervention empowers individuals to recognize, respond to, and prevent abuse in their communities.
examples: Pauline Omuga: The mother is opposed to the practice, because she has attended a talk on gender-based violence and is convinced that even if the daughter wants to go through the right of marriage, they should make the decision when they are older enough, that is 18 years and above.
Emily Ayua: I advised her to report the matter to authorities or NGO's that deal with gender-based violence and to see how they can help her and the children.

Mildred Digolo: I am happy that now as a CHW after the WiRED training, I can now teach my community of their rights and the procedure to follow on gender-based violence and am happy that they are getting help from the places where we direct them.
Vincent Ochien'g: We discussed the issue as a group and learned that the first step is to report to the police station then proceed to the hospital within 24 hours of the horrific ordeal.

Liz Adhiambo: In my field work I came about such cases whereby I referred some of them to the facilities but some are still in denial state. On my side I also managed to counsel some of them in which they are in a good state now and they always give me thanks for helping them, making me be happy.
Lency Mmbone: They were very happy to learn a lot of things and promised to report in case of any abuse to 1195 which is the number for health care assistance Kenya.

concept: Empowerment through Health Education
rationale: The testimonials consistently highlight the transformative power of health education. The community health workers express a sense of empowerment, confidence, and recognition in their communities as a result of their training. They also emphasize the positive impact of their newfound knowledge on their communities, as they are now able to provide vital health information and services.
examples: Mildred Digolo: With the information I have from the training and my knowledge, the community I am in today is changing gradually.
Daniel Ayieko: My work in the community has elevated me to many county of Kisumu platforms where through the county department of health have accorded me recognition.
Susan Osoik: The CHWs training really changed my life. It helped me to stand before people and talk with confidence because I was well trained with important information for my community.
Milka Opela: The WiRED training was so extensive that I now feel empowered. Being empowered has made me a different person, and I am eager to implement my knowledge in my community.

concept: The Importance and Challenges of Menstrual Hygiene Education
rationale: The testimonials consistently highlight the critical role of education in menstrual hygiene management (MHM) and the challenges faced due to cultural taboos, poverty, and lack of resources. The community health workers (CHWs) are actively involved in educating both women and men about MHM, debunking myths, and providing necessary resources.
examples: Bunnyce Atieno: Menstrual poverty is a major leading factor in this lack of sanitary towels during this time of the month forcing some girls to engage in transactional sex which back to these unwanted teenage pregnancies.

Mildred Digolo: The girl had a bad attitude towards using sanitary pads because her mother had instructed her in using small pieces of cloth during her menses because they were poor and they could not afford to buy pads.

Pauline Adhiambo: I realized that lack of information about menstrual hygiene leads to unhygienic and unhealthy menstrual practices that create misconceptions and negative attitudes which motivates shaming, bullying, and even gender based violence.
Lency Mmbone: The 14 members of the group expressed how they don't participate in MHM at the household level, stating that it was a taboo for men from their community to even talk about menstruation.

concept: Health Misconceptions and Lifestyle Changes
rationale: The testimonials consistently highlight the community health workers' efforts to correct health misconceptions and promote lifestyle changes as a means to prevent and manage various health conditions. These include obesity, hypertension, high blood pressure, ulcers, and breast cancer.
examples: NO NAME (unknown, 2020-2022) on Obesity: I told her the only thing she needed was exercise and a change of diet and she would be okay.
Pauline Adhiambo (Female, 3/2023) on Hypertension: We have been advocating for lifestyle changes which include weight loss, increased physical activities and dietary changes.
Zachary Omondi (Male, 3/2023) on Hypertension: We informed our participants to regularly check their blood pressure so that in case of any problem they can get medical attention as soon as possible.
Imelda Anyango (Female, 6/2023) on Misinformation about Ulcers: I taught them that anybody is at risk of getting ulcers due to one's lifestyle and can determine if one can stay healthy or not.

Daniel Ayieko (Male, 11/2024) on Physical Fitness: I took them through the benefits of physical fitness. Concerning physical health, the exercises help in reducing the risk of chronic diseases such as diabetes, heart disease, and obesity through strengthening the immune system as well as improving bone density and muscle health.

concept: Perceived Impact of Family Planning Methods on Women's Health
rationale: Across the testimonials, a recurring theme is the perceived impact of different family planning methods on women's health, particularly in relation to infertility, menstrual irregularities, and fibroids. The community health workers discuss the community's beliefs, fears, and experiences with these methods, highlighting the need for more education and awareness.
examples: Tracy Agatha Achieng': Infertility is a major problem in the community. Some women are accused by their spouses to be infertile because people believe men cannot be infertile. Others say that some infertility causes are caused by contraceptives such as pills and family planning method which is Depo.
Bunnyce Atieno: So many women are partaking in family planning methods and the most loved the implant. Many people have different reactions to the method they prefer most.

Tracy Agatha Achieng': It has come to our attention that a number of women are experiencing fibroids and have different perspectives about its existence. Upon sharing with some women, it seems that they think it (fibroids) comes about with the family planning methods which are being used.

Steve Wonder: When sensitization about health issues started, most mothers accepted family planning. Quite a number of them opted for long-term family planning methods and they say this has given them a chance to take care of the existing children.

concept: The Power of Nutrition Education
rationale: Across the testimonials, a common theme is the transformative impact of nutrition education on community health. Community health workers often encounter misconceptions or lack of knowledge about nutrition, but through their efforts to educate and raise awareness, they are able to guide individuals towards healthier dietary choices and practices.
examples: Mildred Digolo: As CHW, I am thankful to KUAP, as they offer nutrition programs and teaching to young mothers on how they can handle their little ones.
Imelda Anyango: I advised him in love, not reminding him of what he said some months ago and was happy.
Milka Nyadiang'a: The lady was very happy and promised to continue feeding the children a healthy diet containing all the required nutrients that helps in growth and development.

Pauline Adhiambo: The people who I taught this idea of kitchen garden are very happy since it occupies a small plot size, located close to the homestead, having diversity of crops and easily adaptable by the poor with limited resources.
Liz Adhiambo: I had to take my audience through the module to teach them the foods that help in replacement of iron every time they lose blood.

concept: Empowerment through Health Education and Intervention
rationale: The testimonials consistently highlight the role of community health workers in educating community members about various health conditions, identifying symptoms, and guiding them towards appropriate medical intervention. This process empowers community members to understand their health better and take necessary actions.
examples: Daniel Ayieko: During my field work, I came across two people who were coughing as I was training them. I asked them when they started coughing and advised them to see the doctor for a tuberculosis test.
Bunnyce Atieno: The importance that I had shared with the community was to know how to treat the disease, to know the preventive measures, to know the signs and symptoms.
Linet Awuor: At the end of the session the audience understood the prevention measures in regard to TB. They also understood that TB can be treated.

Nelly Oyule: As a CHW I convinced him and took time to talk to him. So in our conversation I found out he had symptoms of arthritis, so I asked him if he knew what arthritis is. Unfortunately he didn't know, so I informed him that it is an infection caused by a fault in the immune system.

concept: The Power of Education and Dialogue in Community Health
rationale: Across the testimonials, community health workers consistently highlight the importance of education and open dialogue in addressing various health issues. They emphasize the transformative power of knowledge and conversation in changing attitudes, behaviors, and outcomes related to topics like drug abuse, mental health, and reproductive health.
examples: Bunnyce Atieno: I talked to a group of young girls who agreed to open up about their abortion experience and none of them enjoyed even a bit of it. I agreed with them that there would be no more abortion.
Liz Odhiambo: I managed to talk to them and advised them concerning the bad effects which they could undergo.
Pauline Omuga: As I was teaching about drugs, I realized that much of what people hear about drugs actually comes from those selling them.
Carren Osomo: I had to talk and council them on this then we agreed that we should challenge stigma and provide understanding and compassion towards those struggling with mental health issues.
Imelda Anyango: Ever since I started teaching and giving people advice about mental health, the suicidal cases have decreased.

concept: Empowerment through Health Education and Counseling
rationale: Across the testimonials, community health workers consistently use education and counseling to empower individuals to take control of their health. This includes dispelling misconceptions, providing emotional support, and encouraging individuals to seek professional medical help.
examples: Bunnyce Atieno: I don't know much about fibroids, but the little I know about it managed to cheer her up and build up her self-esteem once again.
Mildred Digolo: I took my time to go and talk to her mother. Though the mother was disappointed, I managed to talk to her and she accepted her daughter back.
Milka Nyadiang'a on Mumps: I took my time and counseled both the mother and her children, who were 13 years, 15 years, and 17 years.
Millicent Randiki on Chicken Pox: After several counseling to the mother she agreed to take her kids to the facility for further treatment.
Linet Awuor on Mental Health: I had a therapy talk together with a counselor whom I referred to help her.
Lency Mmbone on Screening: I mobilized the woman who was always in hospital to treat her children.

Milka Nyadiang'a on Self-Esteem: Such people are being encouraged to stand strongly on their own, know who they want to be and gain courage to talk publicly in public places so as to be strong enough.
Millicent Randiki on Pregnancy: I took her aside after the session, talked to her, and educated her on the benefits of ANC and the disadvantages of buying drugs from the pharmacy.
Imelda Anyango on Depression: I taught her about the signs and symptoms of the condition. I advised her how to manage the sickness and she was so happy.
Milka Nyadiang'a on Depression: As I was having one on one with her she agreed to go and visit a counsellor wand also start her small business to help her support her 3 kids.

concept: Empowerment through Health Education
rationale: Across the testimonials, community health workers consistently share experiences of educating their communities about various health conditions and first aid practices. This education empowers community members to understand, manage, and prevent health issues, leading to improved health outcomes and quality of life.
examples: Liz Adhiambo: I told her how to stop it by: sitting down and firmly pinch the soft part of your nose, just above your nostrils, for at least 10-15 minutes.
Lency Mmbone: After a long discussion with them, I advised them to seek medication, and afterwards practice prevention and good hygiene against their diseases.
Bunnyce Atieno: I told her to go for free cancer screening and now she was diagnosed with breast cancer and is admitted for treatment.
Mary Atieno: I took this personally and took the woman to the hospital. They recommended an ultrasound to find out if it truly was fibroids or any other related disease.

Daniel Ayieko: This has helped me in my field work because I can respond and teach my participants on the mpox disease including symptoms: such as fever, headaches, muscle aches, and rashes that progress from mucus to pustules which form scabs.

concept: Empowerment through Sexual Health Education
rationale: Across the testimonials, community health workers consistently emphasize the importance of educating their communities about sexual health, particularly in relation to HIV/AIDS prevention, teenage pregnancy, and family planning. They highlight the transformative impact of this education, which empowers individuals to make informed decisions about their sexual health and ultimately reduces their risk of contracting sexually transmitted infections or experiencing unintended pregnancies.
examples: Agatha Achieng': I educated the teens on the importance of going for HIV tests with their partners... I solved this by encouraging the teens to go for PREP as it is the only way out to avoid contracting HIV/AIDS since they cannot abstain.
Pauline Odhiambo: I managed to teach them about the importance of using pre-exposure prophylaxis, that is PREPs, for those that were saying they are HIV negative.

Lency Mmbone: During our discussions, they were very happy to know that PEP is pre-exposure prophylaxis... And also we talked about PREP which they knew it was taken after engaging in unprotected sex, so I tried to empower them that PREP is taken by HIV negative people who are at risk of contracting HIV.
Linet Awuor: We discussed how condoms and PREP usage is a way of prevention HIV/AIDS. We discussed how to use a condom and even got a chance to demonstrate with a penile model.

concept: The Importance of Hygiene and Clean Water in Disease Prevention
rationale: Across the testimonials, community health workers consistently emphasize the role of hygiene practices and clean water in preventing diseases like cholera, typhoid, and bilharzia. They highlight the impact of environmental factors such as flooding and industrialization on water safety, and the importance of educating community members on hygiene practices.
examples: Bunnyce Atieno: I taught my audience on how to treat their drinking water using the solar disinfection and also to wash their hands clean to prevent them from contracting cholera.
Tracy Agatha Achieng': The community have been advised not to walk barefooted when it is rainy because they can easily be contaminated with typhoid, cholera and bilharzia.

Daniel Ayieko: I managed to share with them the WiRED cholera module and after sharing many of the participants were very happy for learning new preventive measures against cholera and promised to practice it every day.
Liz Adhiambo: I advised my clients to always make sure that the water they use must be very clean, drinking water more so should be boiled or you can use water guard too purify the water.
Daniel Ayieko: After thorough awareness creation I'm able to witness people washing their hands and also putting up hand washing equipment.

concept: The Importance of Proper Malaria Diagnosis and Treatment
rationale: Across the testimonials, community health workers consistently emphasize the importance of proper diagnosis and treatment for malaria. They highlight the dangers of self-medication and the need for adherence to prescribed treatments. They also stress the importance of preventive measures such as sleeping under treated mosquito nets and maintaining clean surroundings.
examples: Imelda Anyango: Malaria could return again and again because I was not adhering to the instructions of completing doses, I was not treating malaria well, not sleeping under mosquito treated net.
Julliet Omollo: The malaria infection may return time and again if the patient does not follow the preventive measures like sleeping under the treated mosquito nets and vector control.
Daniel Ayieko: I referred the person to Thoamogi Oginga Teaching and Referral Hospital for the malaria test which later turned positive and he was treated and given prescriptions of the medicines.

Bunnyce Atieno: I do advise people with malaria symptoms to go for a test before taking any painkiller, because this can cause danger. I also take an action by taking some of them in hospitals so that they can get treatment.

concept: Empowerment through Health Education
rationale: Across the testimonials, a common theme is the transformative power of health education. Community health workers emphasize the importance of educating community members about various health issues, from HIV/AIDS to basic health practices. This education empowers individuals to make informed decisions about their health, leading to positive changes in behavior and attitudes.
examples: Bunnyce Atieno: I talked to some youths about this and I hope this will be spread in the community to help prevent these deaths.
Vincent Ochien'g: Educating community on the basics of health has helped a lot in the communities we serve a s CHWs.
Mildred Digolo: Educating the community on the basics of health has helped a lot in the communities we serve as CHWs.
Pauline Adhiambo: This is an area which still needs a lot of efforts by CHWs , in order to prevent more of sexual related issues from affecting the community.
Liz Adhiambo: The community has been receiving health education and information on different health issues. They have been also gaining skills of life and this has helped them a lot.

concept: Promotion of Personal Hygiene
rationale: The testimonials from the community health workers revolve around the importance of personal hygiene, specifically menstrual hygiene and prevention of fungal infections. They provide detailed advice on how to maintain cleanliness and prevent health issues related to poor hygiene.
examples: Nelly Oyule: To manage this situation you should use pads. Cotton wool, reusable pads or a piece of cloth. After some hours you change the pads and piece of cloth etc. Don't use the pads for a long time because it gets so soaked it causes rashes on your skin and movement won't be easy.

Liz Adhiambo: It is advisable to get a bath earlier before the time that you want to go somewhere to allow your body to get dry well. After bathing thoroughly, dry you with a clean towel, you will be fresh and remain clean often. Wash your inner pants each time you bath and hang it on a cloth line on the sun to get rid of germs and to help you to be clean at all times.
